title: Compass Cuecraft — Prompt Lab Notes
body:
Goal: iterate fast on a small internal technique I’m calling 'Compass' — a lightweight prompt scaffolding pattern to orient models when they drift across domains. This doc is a scratchpad: hypothesis checks, quick templates, few-shot sets, and failure cases. Not polished. Use, then prune.

High-level idea (one-liner): prefix with an anchored compass (domain cue + goal cue + negative anchor) that is short (8-18 tokens) and followed by an optional exemplar block (0-3 examples) and then the user query. The compass is intentionally compact to preserve token budget while giving the model an explicit guardrail.

Why: too many full-context few-shot patterns blow tokens and still leak ambiguity. Compass trades a small, high-signal anchor for larger context windows.

Quick template skeleton (placeholder syntax):

[COMPASS: DOMAIN="{domain}" | GOAL="{goal}" | AVOID="{avoid_list}" ]\n\n[EXEMPLARS]\n- Input: {ex1_input}\n  Output: {ex1_output}\n- Input: {ex2_input}\n  Output: {ex2_output}\n\nUser: {user_prompt}\nAssistant:

Notes: keep COMPASS on one line if possible. Use pipe separators so it's machine-parseable for tooling.

Small experiments (run id format: compass-YYMMDD-x):
- compass-250618-1: domain=customer-support | goal=concise-answer | avoid=apology-verbosity | exemplars=1
  - Prompt: see skeleton; exemplar shows short FAQ style Q/A.
  - Observed: model over-explains on edge cases; apology still present ~30%.
  - Hypothesis: 'avoid' token list too soft. Try stronger negative exemplar (explicit counterexample) and remove safe apology phrases from exemplar outputs.

- compass-250701-3: domain=finance-blurb | goal=plain-english-summary | avoid=jargon | exemplars=2
  - Observed: improved on jargon rate, but hallucinated numbers in 12% of cases when asked to summarize long inputs.
  - Next step: add 'verify-numbers: no invention' as micro-rule in COMPASS.

Exemplar design rules (working):
- Use 1–2 exemplars for low-latency flows; 3 only for brittle tasks.
- Exemplars should be contrastive: one good, one subtle-bad (helps boundary learning).
- Avoid including long raw source text inside exemplars—summaries only.

Failure case catalogue (notes-to-self):
- F1: Negative anchor ignored when the user prompt contradicts it (model obeys user more). Mitigation: echo the COMPASS constraint in the assistant prelude ("Following the constraint: {AVOID}").
- F2: Token budget bleed when domain cue repeated in exemplar. Mitigation: collapsible tokens — use abbreviations in exemplars and include full expansion in COMPASS only.
- F3: Overfit to exemplar format (repeats exact wording). Mitigation: diversifying language in exemplars + light paraphrase augmentation.

Mini-heuristics to test (short checklist):
- [ ] Does adding a 1-token anchor word (e.g., "BRIEF:") change length distribution? track mean tokens.
- [ ] Compare temperature 0.0 vs 0.2 on refusal rate for 'avoid' instructions.
- [ ] Try anchor as "soft" vs "hard" (polite phrasing vs explicit instruction) and measure compliance.

Concrete prompt variants to A/B (copy/paste for runner):

Variant A (soft-negative):
COMPASS: DOMAIN="sales-email" | GOAL="short pitch" | AVOID="disallowed-pii, long history"
\nUser: Draft a 3-sentence outreach for a VP of product about autoscaling savings.
Assistant:

Variant B (hard-negative + echo):
COMPASS: DOMAIN="sales-email" | GOAL="short pitch" | AVOID="DO NOT MENTION CUSTOMER NAMES OR FINANCIAL FIGURES"
\nAssistant Preamble: "Will follow constraints: DO NOT MENTION CUSTOMER NAMES OR FINANCIAL FIGURES. Reply in 3 sentences."
\nUser: Draft a 3-sentence outreach for a VP of product about autoscaling savings.
Assistant:

Observed so far: B reduces hallucinated figures but increases stilted phrasing. Trade-off acceptable for compliance-sensitive flows.

Metrics I want to capture for each run (minimal):
- token_cost (input+output)
- compliance_rate (binary per-example w/ heuristics + spot human eval)
- avg_response_tokens
- latency_p50/p95
- observed-hallucination-rate (human-annotated sample)

Open questions / hypotheses to test next:
- Is COMPASS more effective when surfaced as a JSON metadata blob vs human-readable line? (e.g., {"domain":"X","goal":"Y"}) — try both; instrumentation easier with JSON.
- Can we distill COMPASS into a single learned system message for dedicated deployments (Redwood Dedicated) to avoid repeating per-request costs? Risks: cross-user contamination; must be per-tenant.
- Negative exemplars: is it better to include a single explicit negative example (bad -> corrected) or to use a list of avoidance phrases? Early sign: explicit negative example helps for syntactic errors; phrase list helps for content hallucination.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Run compass-260201-1 batch across 500 support Qs, compare compliance to baseline prompt-set v3.
- [ ] Add automated detection heuristics for 'apology' and 'hallucinated-figure' in evaluation scripts (see linked PR).
- [ ] Draft short blurb for Prompt Library README describing COMPASS pattern (1 paragraph + 1 example).

Loose snippets / quick wins:
- Use separators like '---' after COMPASS to reduce model copying the anchor verbatim.
- For multi-turn tasks, include 'TURN=1' in COMPASS and let assistant append 'TURN=<n+1>' when responding; helps routing in pipeline.

References and context:
- Related ticket: CONF-PL-412 (prompt library indexing / metadata). 
- Local tooling: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-tools/pull/88 contains a small parser for COMPASS-line to auto-fill structured metadata.
- Slack notes: thread CLDR9K2B3 — early user complaints about apology-length in support replies.

Final note: this is exploratory. Keep exemplars short, make 'avoid' explicit but test polite vs imperative phrasing. When in doubt, prioritize compliance for regulated domains (finance/health) even if style suffers. Will iterate after the 500-sample batch.

-- Avery (scratchpad)\n
Questions for Imani before next run: do we have existing human eval capacity next week? If not, I’ll run a smaller seed of 100 samples and flag borderline cases for manual review.\n
-- end
